findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated.
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract methods (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). This subclass is just `pass`, so creating it raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. If `MetricAlertFire` registers this class as its `detector_handler`, then `Detector.detector_handler` will raise for any `metric_alert_fire` detector. That crashes `process_detectors` for the whole batch. Before this change the handler safely returned no results. I could not see how the handler is instantiated, so this assumes `detector_handler` constructs it directly. Fix: keep a concrete stub that implements the abstract methods, for example returning empty values or raising `NotImplementedError` only inside those methods, or keep it on `DetectorHandler` with `evaluate` returning `{}` until the stateful version is built.

findings.title: Expected occurrence is built for group key "val1" but the evaluated group key is "group_key".
findings.body: `evaluate_group_key_value` is called with `expected_result.group_key == "group_key"`, so the handler's occurrence gets the fingerprint `build_fingerprint("group_key")`. The expected occurrence here uses `"val1"`, so its fingerprint is different. `IssueOccurrence` is compared by value, so the equality assertion fails, unless the test only exercises the dedupe skip path in the part not shown. Build the expected occurrence with `"group_key"` instead.
